s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with tremors, weakness, and gait instability
salient_findings: Episodes of spasms and tremors in the right hand and forearm
Extensive nonenhancing lesions in the bilateral cerebral hemispheres on MRI
key_facts: Woman in her mid-60s
Initial presentation with episodes of spasms and tremors in the right hand and forearm
Underwent carpal tunnel release surgery
Tremors recurred 7 months later
Developed progressive right-sided weakness, dysarthria, hand tremors, slurred speech, and gait instability over 3 months
Brain MRI showed hyperintensities throughout the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter, corpus callosum, basal ganglia, thalami, midbrain, upper pons, and middle cerebellar peduncles
T1-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery MRI with contrast showed absence of contrast enhancement
Brain biopsy revealed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ EBV/EBER− cells
Cerebrospinal fluid contained lymphoma cells
Bone marrow was negative for lymphoma cells

shortlist.label: Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Brain biopsy revealed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ EBV/EBER− cells and cerebrospinal fluid contained lymphoma cells

shortlist.label: Intravascular Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological decline with tremors, weakness, and gait instability, and presence of lymphoma cells in cerebrospinal fluid

shortlist.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Brain MRI showed hyperintensities throughout the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter, corpus callosum, basal ganglia, thalami, midbrain, upper pons, and middle cerebellar peduncles

shortlist.label: Multiple Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Brain MRI showed hyperintensities throughout the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter, corpus callosum, basal ganglia, thalami, midbrain, upper pons, and middle cerebellar peduncles

shortlist.label: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological decline with tremors, weakness, and gait instability, and brain MRI showed hyperintensities throughout the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter

raw.rationale: The presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid and the brain biopsy showing CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ EBV/EBER− cells, along with the absence of systemic lymphoma (negative bone marrow), supports the diagnosis of Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma.

rejected.label: Intravascular Lymphoma
rejected.why: Intravascular lymphoma typically presents with systemic symptoms and is less likely to cause localized neurological deficits.

rejected.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
rejected.why: PML is caused by JC virus infection and typically occurs in immunocompromised patients, with a different pathological and imaging profile.

rejected.label: Multiple Sclerosis
rejected.why: MS is an autoimmune disease with a relapsing-remitting course, and the presence of lymphoma cells is not consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
rejected.why: ADEM is a monophasic illness with a distinct clinical and imaging profile, and the presence of lymphoma cells is not consistent with this diagnosis.
